applicability_conditions: The test medium is aqueous and contains available iron(III).
The phenolic hydroxy group is structurally accessible.
The observed colour is distinct from the iron(III) reagent blank.
rule.claim: In aqueous media where iron(III) remains available for coordination, an accessible phenolic hydroxy group can form a visibly colored iron(III)-phenol or iron(III)-phenolate complex.
exclusions: This forward rule is not an unconditional colour-implies-phenol inverse.
A negative result does not exclude every phenol.
Precipitation, incompatible pH, or competing strong ligands are outside scope.
The rule does not identify a particular molecule.

source.locator: Nature 165 (1950) 1012, complete one-page letter; absorption and titration study of freshly prepared aqueous ferric chloride-phenol coloured complexes.

applicability_conditions: The problem statement supplies a finite and explicitly closed candidate set.
Every candidate has been audited for accessible phenolic hydroxy groups.

For every candidate lacking an accessible phenolic hydroxy group, in-scope non-phenolic iron(III)-chromogenic mechanisms and incompatible test conditions have been affirmatively ruled out from source-given structures or facts and trusted registry rules; mere failure to find an interferent is insufficient.
The problem statement itself, rather than the solver, describes the observed aqueous iron(III) response as characteristic.
rule.claim: For an explicitly closed candidate set supplied by the problem statement, after a complete candidate-structure audit and affirmative exclusion of in-scope non-phenolic iron(III)-chromogenic mechanisms and incompatible test conditions, a response that the problem statement itself describes as characteristic may be used only as a bounded discriminating cue to retain candidates with an accessible phenolic hydroxy group.
exclusions: This policy is not a universal colour-implies-phenol chemical law.
It does not identify an open-world unknown.
It does not authorize inference when candidate coverage or interference exclusion is incomplete.
It does not use a negative test to exclude every phenol.
The cited study reports selectivity only for its tested paint-and-resin panel and protocol; it does not itself establish this policy for arbitrary candidate domains.

source.locator: Journal of the Japan Society of Colour Material 35(2) (1962) 59-61; page 59 abstract and page 61 discussion and conclusion, limited to the tested paint-and-resin panel and protocol.

applicability_conditions: The material has been independently established as ideal stoichiometric mellite using a separately pinned mellite_ideal_stoichiometry receipt.
The problem source explicitly states thermogravimetric heating in open air and a final residue mass that remains stable at higher temperatures, with an exact source locator recorded for each cue.

A source-bound derivation from the problem data, separately pinned qualitative evidence, and the complete candidate audit affirmatively establishes complete conversion to a terminal phase; mass stability alone is insufficient.

The problem source or an independently source-bound derivation establishes that aluminium and oxygen are the only nonvolatile elements available to the terminal residue; every possible counterion, dopant, container, or atmosphere contribution has been affirmatively excluded.

A closed candidate audit enumerates every charge-neutral integer formula composed only of trivalent aluminium and divalent oxygen and checks each candidate against atom, charge, and measured-mass intervals using pinned constants and source uncertainties.
The separately pinned Treccani Mellite source is used only as qualitative corroboration that established mellite can leave an infusible alumina residue in a blowpipe test.
rule.claim: Within an explicitly closed problem domain satisfying every listed condition, a neutral integer formula candidate composed only of trivalent aluminium and divalent oxygen may be retained as a terminal-residue candidate when it passes the complete atom, charge, and measured-mass interval audit.
exclusions: This bounded policy is not a paper or a universal empirical calcination law.
It does not identify an open-world residue and does not authorize inference when any activation cue, candidate, ledger entry, or uncertainty bound is missing or ambiguous.
The Treccani blowpipe observation does not itself establish open-air thermogravimetric conditions, complete conversion, quantitative recovery, or a temperature-time program.
It does not authorize any specific calcination or thermogravimetric temperature, duration, yield, purity, phase, or polymorph.
It does not authorize selection from mass agreement alone, and no ambiguous-atmosphere trace may be used as evidence for an open-air cue.

source.locator: Piazza, Mellite, Enciclopedia Italiana (1934), sentence reporting that mellite burns in a blowpipe test and leaves an infusible alumina residue. Normalized Italian sentence SHA-256: 5b58d1ef840834a81224de8487fde93c4f09ef2ed4643f70f0e530cdc76357a5.

applicability_conditions: The substrate is exactly hexamethylbenzene.
The oxidant is potassium permanganate.
The reported cold-condition transformation is the claimed scope.
rule.claim: Under the reported cold potassium-permanganate conditions, hexamethylbenzene can be oxidized to mellitic acid.
exclusions: The record does not establish an acidic medium.
It does not generalize to arbitrary alkylbenzenes.
It does not claim a unique product, rate, or yield outside the reported protocol.

source.locator: Bulletin de la Société minéralogique de France 4 (1881) 26-28, page 26 opening paragraph.

applicability_conditions: The phase has been independently established as crystalline mellite.
The material is treated as an ideal stoichiometric phase.
rule.claim: The ideal crystalline mineral mellite has composition Al2[C6(COO)6]·16H2O, equivalently [Al(H2O)6]2·C12O12·4H2O.
exclusions: Occurrence in a coal or lignite deposit alone does not identify a sample.
Impure or nonstoichiometric material is outside scope.
This rule does not determine a thermal-decomposition residue.

source.locator: Acta Crystallographica B29 (1973) 26-31, page 26 abstract and reported single-crystal composition.

applicability_conditions: The substrate is mellitic acid.
The dehydrating reagent and heating protocol are the reported benzoyl-chloride procedure.
rule.claim: In the reported six-hour heating protocol with a large excess of benzoyl chloride, mellitic acid undergoes complete dehydration to C12O9; warm-water hydration by three water equivalents regenerates the acid.
exclusions: This record does not authorize substitution of phosphorus pentoxide.
It does not generalize to arbitrary polycarboxylic acids or dehydrating reagents.

source.locator: Berichte der deutschen chemischen Gesellschaft 46 (1913) 813-815; page 814 preparation and page 815 hydration and analysis.

applicability_conditions: The substrate is exactly mellitic acid.
The reagent is exactly phosphorus pentoxide and the mixture is heated.
The product reference is limited to the mellitic trianhydride identified by the immediately preceding discussion in the cited paper.
The claim is existential and partial: the paper's 'some' product formation is the maximum admitted extent.
rule.claim: When mellitic acid is heated with phosphorus pentoxide under the reported conditions, some mellitic trianhydride (C12O9) forms.
exclusions: The record does not establish complete or quantitative dehydration, conversion, yield, or mass balance.
It does not establish that C12O9 is the sole or principal product, or that pure trianhydride can be isolated by this procedure.
It does not generalize to another substrate, dehydrating reagent, or unreported protocol.
It is not a thermal-decomposition rule and does not identify any open-air thermogravimetric residue.

source.locator: Meyer and Steiner, Monatshefte für Chemie 35 (1914) 475–518, printed pp. 512–513: p. 512 identifies the antecedent as the trianhydride; p. 513 reports that P2O5-heating forms some of that anhydride and then limits its preparative utility.
